problem: The scope names what the characterization covers and where its run lives, but four of its nodes rest on a choice the sources do not make.

questions.text: fc launch new creates its own folder, flightdeck/launch/<spec.name>-1/, beside the new-layout folder that holds this spec. Where does this launch's run live?
questions.why: The v1 tooling copies the spec into a launch folder it names and resolves the active launch by scanning for launch.json; the new-layout folder already carries one.

options.value: Accept the sibling v1 folder as the run's home; the new-layout folder keeps the spec series and interview only, and nothing is retrofitted.
Something else: say how the run should be opened.

questions.text: When a characterization test finds that a kept part behaves wrongly today, what does the suite do?
questions.why: Standard characterization pins what the system does, not what it should do; the rebuild then knows the wart is there. Skipping loses the coverage; fixing contradicts the no-change rule.

options.value: Pin the current behaviour as the passing case, with a note in the suite naming it as a defect to carry to the core spec.
Leave that case out and record the defect in the run report for the core spec to absorb.
Fix it in this launch after all; SC10 is loosened to allow defect repairs.

questions.text: Thirty tracked suites already exist and most test the runner's commands rather than the observable boundary. How do they relate to the characterization suites?
questions.why: A boundary-level tracked suite is already a characterization; a runner-shaped one proves the wrong thing and would be deleted with the runner.

options.value: Reference a tracked suite where it already proves the behaviour at the boundary; write a fresh suite only where the tracked one is runner-shaped.
Write a fresh characterization suite for every kept part regardless, so the set stands on its own when the runner suites go.

questions.text: No hooks are installed in this project's .claude/settings.json today. How are the enforcement behaviours characterized?
questions.why: The existing hooks-* suites drive each hook script with a synthetic event and read its decision; a live session would prove the wiring too but is agent-shaped and slow.

options.value: Drive the hook scripts with synthetic events, as the tracked hooks-* suites do; the wiring into settings is the rebuild's install step, not a kept behaviour.
Install the settings fragment first and characterize through a live Claude Code session as well.

questions.text: The spec chain and the crew are agent-shaped. How far does their characterization go?
questions.why: Role files, dispatch rendering and return shapes are deterministic; the judge's verdicts are not. The rubric bench under flightdeck/testbench/benches/rubrics/spec/ already holds human-graded drafts, so one judged check has golden material without a new grading session.

options.value: Deterministic only: frontmatter, dispatch rendering, return shapes, rubric and template bytes; no live agent runs in this launch.
Deterministic plus one judged check: a live spec-judge run over the bench's graded drafts, its verdict sheet compared to the bench's human grades.
Live checks for every agent-shaped role, each with its own scenario set.
